clue.text: Very fine one, a capital city

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone praises a capital city as very fine indeed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofia is the capital of Bulgaria.

clue.text: House over in Lime Street

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned upside down, so the letters run bottom to top
the letters sit inside the words that follow, so read them from within the phrase

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A house is said to be over in Lime Street, the Liverpool address.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is short for a semi-detached house, a common British home sharing one wall with its neighbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Semi is the everyday British abbreviation for a semi-detached dwelling.

clue.text: Senior politician from abroad, clergyman

parts.note: foreign means from another country
a minister is a member of the clergy

explanation.surface: A senior politician turns out to be a clergyman from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: Minister works in both senses: the clerical one in the wordplay and the governmental one in the whole answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreign minister is a senior cabinet member handling relations with other countries.

clue.text: A series under discussion

parts.note: taken as written
a tissue is a connected series, as in 'a tissue of lies'

explanation.surface: A series of programmes is being discussed.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter at issue is the point currently being debated or disputed.

clue.text: Occasionally available in a little Square in New York City?

definitions.text: available in a little Square in New York City?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words: a few copies of a newspaper you might buy in Times Square

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words and it describes a few copies of the paper that gives Times Square its name; the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means at intervals, not always; the split form means a number of newspapers.

clue.text: Father's name for a fascinating woman

parts.note: a sire is a father, especially of an animal
N is the standard abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A father has a pet name for an alluring woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Father means 'has', joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth the Sirens lured sailors with song, so a siren is a seductive, captivating woman.

clue.text: Give incorrect gen to short schoolgirl in class

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the final letter of the next word is dropped

parts.note: a schoolgirl is a miss
taken as written
a form is a school class in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone gives wrong information to a little schoolgirl in her class.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information; a form is a school year group or class.
explanation.definitionFit: To misinform is to supply someone with wrong information.

clue.text: Una drops out of sporting competition in agony

indicators.note: a name dropping out of something leaves it, so those letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be removed
a tournament is a sporting competition

explanation.surface: A competitor called Una withdraws from a tournament in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: Take U, N and A out of TOURNAMENT and TORMENT is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment and agony are synonyms for severe suffering.

clue.text: Moderate fielder had to do, running after last of them

indicators.note: running suggests letters moving about freely, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, all fourteen letters

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of them

explanation.surface: A cricketer had chores to do, chasing after the rest of the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderate fielder' looks like a mid-on or mid-off, but the fielder is just letters for the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle-of-the-road describes views that avoid extremes, which is what moderate means.

clue.text: Female singer showing tension, appearing after boy, leader of group

parts.note: a son is a boy

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of group
stress is tension

explanation.surface: A female vocalist looks tense when she follows a boy who leads the band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appearing after' places the tension piece after the boy and the group letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A songstress is a woman who sings, especially professionally.

clue.text: Spoil artist put in lodgings for festival

parts.note: to mar is to spoil

indicators.note: something put in another thing goes inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: digs is British slang for rented lodgings
RA, Royal Academician, a stock crossword artist

explanation.surface: An artist moves into lodgings and ruins them before a festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Mardi Gras is the Shrove Tuesday carnival celebrated in New Orleans and elsewhere.

clue.text: Element causing trouble among our sailors

indicators.note: one thing among others is surrounded by them, so it goes inside

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's own sailors
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: Something stirs up trouble among a ship's crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Radon is a radioactive gas, a chemical element in the periodic table.

clue.text: End endless pain, getting treatment for complaint

indicators.note: letters getting treatment are worked on and reshaped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, all fourteen letters

explanation.surface: A sufferer wants to stop chronic pain by getting medical treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' tempts you to cut a letter, but here it is plain fodder, every letter used.
explanation.definitionFit: Pins and needles is the tingling ailment felt when a limb has gone numb.

clue.text: A warning sign? Meet with doctor

parts.note: paths cross when they meet
Bones is a nickname for a doctor, from sawbones

explanation.surface: A sign warns someone to go and see a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: skull and crossbones warn of poison or pirates.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossed bones under a skull are a traditional symbol cautioning of deadly danger.

clue.text: Poem and piece of music heard

indicators.note: heard means the word is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: a rondo is a musical form with a recurring theme

explanation.surface: A poem and a piece of music are performed together.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondeau is a French verse form of thirteen lines on two rhymes with a refrain.

clue.text: Let a nun be maltreated? That's indefensible

indicators.note: something maltreated is knocked about, so the letters are roughly rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Allowing a nun to suffer abuse could never be justified.
explanation.definitionFit: An untenable position cannot be held or justified, so it is indefensible.

clue.text: Get the better of other ranks in the open air

parts.note: to outdo is to surpass
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: An officer outdoes the soldiers on an outdoor exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdoor activities take place outside, under the sky rather than in a building.

clue.text: One used by downhill racers on their way to the top?

definitions.text: One used by downhill racers on their way to the top?

parts.words: One used by downhill racers on their way to the top?
parts.note: surface reading: a tactic or helper that ambitious athletes use to rise to the top of their sport

parts.words: on their way to the top
parts.note: setter's reading: literally carried up the mountain before the descent

explanation.walkthrough: 'On their way to the top' sounds like career success, but it means physically going up a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiers ride a mechanical tow or chair up the slope before racing down it.

clue.text: Sceptical in chess federation over Lasker's opening

parts.note: taken as written
FIDE is the international chess federation

indicators.note: a word's opening is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the world champion's name

explanation.surface: A doubter in the chess world questions champion Lasker's choice of opening.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' puts the federation above the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Infidel as an adjective means unbelieving, rejecting a faith, close to sceptical.

clue.text: Most of team must, suffering changes

indicators.note: suffering suggests being knocked out of shape, so letters are rearranged
most of a word is all but its final letter, so that letter goes

parts.note: taken as written, before trimming
taken as written

explanation.surface: Most of the team must put up with changes.
explanation.walkthrough: Trim TEAM to TEA, add MUST, then mix all seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutates and changes are both verbs for altering form.

clue.text: Terriers drank rum with pot

indicators.note: rum means odd or peculiar, so the letters come out in a strange order

parts.note: the Terriers is a nickname for the Territorial Army, TA
the letters of drank rearranged

explanation.surface: Some dogs drank rum out of a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terriers' looks like dogs, and 'rum' like a drink, but they are the army reservists and the mixing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankard is a large drinking mug, and pot is a term for such a vessel of beer.

clue.text: Film barrister attending hostile meeting

parts.note: a brief is informal British slang for a lawyer
an encounter can be a clash or confrontation

explanation.surface: A barrister turns up at a confrontational meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief Encounter is David Lean's 1945 British romantic movie set around a railway station.

clue.text: Drop of ouzo when one's in watering hole

indicators.note: a drop is the smallest amount, so just the first letter of the drink

parts.note: the first letter of the Greek spirit

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the letters around it

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
the Roman numeral for one
the possessive ending supplies its letter

explanation.surface: A drinker takes a drop of ouzo at the local bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watering hole' suggests a pub, but here it is the literal desert spring.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile spot in a desert where water is found.

clue.text: About to take off cloak

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
to take off someone is to mimic them, to ape them

explanation.surface: Someone is about to remove a cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' looks like removing clothes, fitting the cloak, but it means imitate.
explanation.definitionFit: A cape is a sleeveless outer garment, a short cloak.

clue.text: Well-known record, Dylan's first

parts.note: to note is to record

indicators.note: the first of a name is its initial, so only that is kept

parts.note: the initial of Dylan

explanation.surface: Bob Dylan's debut is a celebrated album.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' suggests an LP, but here it is the verb meaning write down.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means famous or distinguished, the same as well-known.

clue.text: Dance master, a bright star

parts.note: a boss is a master
taken as written
a nova is a star that suddenly flares in brightness

explanation.surface: A dance master is a shining star.
explanation.definitionFit: Bossa nova is a Brazilian dance and musical style related to samba.

clue.text: More than one itinerant in street waves

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
rollers are long heavy waves

explanation.surface: A wandering person waves at passers-by in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Strollers are people who wander or walk leisurely, roaming like itinerants.

clue.text: Western city to avoid

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... City, the Kansas frontier town of cowboy films
second meaning: to evade or sidestep

explanation.walkthrough: 'Western' with a capital hints at the film genre: Dodge City is the classic Wild West town.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the Kansas cowtown and is also a verb for evading something.
